claims.text: Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi has a homogeneous, soft, single-phase FCC structure.
Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi contains inherent porosity.
CoCrFeNiTi tends to form brittle HCP phases during slow cooling or high-temperature exposure.
High-energy milling at about 400 rpm for 4 h with cooling intervals is an applicable powder-processing regime.
SPS at 1050–1100 °C and 30–40 MPa with a dwell of no more than about 10 min is an applicable consolidation regime.
A heating rate above 50 °C/min throughout SPS is required for the proposed outcome.
High-energy milling introduces severe lattice distortion and a high dislocation density in CoCrFeNiTi.
Rapid SPS under the proposed conditions suppresses porosity in milled CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed process produces a fine-grained structure dominated by FCC with a minor BCC fraction.
Rapid processing suppresses formation of a brittle HCP phase in CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed process suppresses Nb-rich Laves phase formation.
Keeping the displacement rate below 10 µm/min during the densification plateau minimizes grain growth.
Controlling displacement during SPS prevents thermal-expansion-mismatch cracking.
Milling-induced defects lower the activation energy for FCC stability and inhibit HCP and Laves phase nucleation.
High defect density and solute drag stabilize FCC in the rapidly sintered alloy.
Short thermal exposure prevents diffusion-controlled HCP or Laves phase formation and limits grain coarsening.
The processed alloy will have less than 1% porosity and a grain size below 500 nm.
The processed alloy will have a Vickers hardness above 300 HV.
Temperatures above approximately 1150 °C promote rapid HCP nucleation, while dwell times above 20 min permit diffusion-driven phase separation.
Load- and dwell-dependent nanoindentation from 10 to 100 mN and 1 to 100 s can distinguish grain-refinement hardening from solute strengthening.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts suppression of an Nb-rich Laves phase even though the stated CoCrFeNiTi system and processing additions contain no Nb.
The operating regime requires a dwell time strictly below 10 min, but the principal rapid-SPS sample in the falsification experiment is held for 10 min.

The falsification rule says that increased HCP or Laves formation after a 60 min dwell or slow heating would falsify the hypothesis, although that result would support the hypothesis's claim that rapid, short processing is essential for suppressing those phases.
